# Results — Study 842 (Implementation Shortfall): the paper-vs-live cost gap

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). This is a **research-method
demo**: we take the SAME moderate-turnover cross-sectional strategy — a signal we *planted*
to carry a genuine gross edge, so its 0-cost "paper" Sharpe honestly dazzles — and evaluate
it across a ladder of transaction costs (0 / optimistic / realistic / stressed) with a
turnover-scaled market-impact term (~ participation). Fully offline & deterministic; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. Stamped as-of 2026-06-30 (a stamp date;
a synthetic tape carries no calendar of its own). Fingerprint `79082a088002` (planted returns
panel; config: 30 names × 2,520 days, edge=0.0005, persistence φ=0.96, frac=0.2, seed=842;
null panel `87551053f9a3`).*

## The verdict, earned — Signal `NONE` · Tradability `MIRAGE` · "Does ignoring costs manufacture the edge?" `CONFIRMED`

A backtest without a cost model is meaningless. On this tape the paper portfolio (0 cost)
posts a **gross Sharpe of 2.27** (NW *t* = **+7.65**, ≈ +30.9%/yr) — a number a naive
backtester would call a real edge. But the same book rotates ~35% of NAV a day, and once you
charge the friction of that trading the alpha evaporates: at a **realistic** cost it is
**net Sharpe 0.24** (net *t* = **+0.79** — no longer significant), and under **stressed**
costs it **loses money** (net Sharpe −1.78). And it dies *as a function of turnover*: hold the
gross edge fixed and crank the trading, and the identical paper alpha goes from net Sharpe
**+1.40** (slow signal) to **−15.54** (fast signal). The synthetic-only nature of the tape
caps the SIGNAL axis at `NONE`; the costed book is a `MIRAGE`; the myth — that ignoring costs
manufactures the edge — is `CONFIRMED`.

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Tape | **synthetic, offline, deterministic** — no real market data, no network, no cache |
| Panel | 30 names × 2,520 business days (2010-01-04 →, decorative index), seed 842 |
| Signal | per-name latent **unit-variance AR(1)**, persistence φ; the next-day return loads on the **lagged** signal `r_{i,t} = edge·s_{i,t-1} + 0.015·η` |
| Edge knob | `edge = 0.0005` plants the gross paper alpha; `edge = 0` is the null (nothing gross to find) |
| Turnover knob | φ (AR(1)) sets the turnover with the gross edge held fixed: φ→1 ⇒ low turnover, φ→0 ⇒ high turnover |
| Book | dollar-neutral equal-weight long-top-20% / short-bottom-20%, signal known at close `t−1` (one `shift`), held day `t` |
| Cost model | `net = gross − turnover·cost_bps − impact_coef_bps·turnover²` — a **linear** one-way cost + a **super-linear** market-impact term (~ participation) |
| Statistics | Newey-West (HAC, 10-lag) *t* on the daily spread (gross & net); annualised Sharpe; the cost ladder; the break-even cost; the turnover curve; a 20-seed synthetic control |

**Why synthetic-only (named on the SIGNAL axis).** The whole point is a *known* gross edge with
a *known* turnover, so the cost model's bite is unambiguous. Real free data can never certify a
clean planted gross edge, so this method demo is capped at `NONE` — it can never earn `REAL`
(which requires a robust *t* ≥ 2 on a **real** tape).

## The headline — the same strategy, four cost worlds

Moderate turnover (φ = 0.96 ⇒ **0.348**/day one-way), n = **2,519** days:

| scenario | one-way / impact | gross Sharpe | net Sharpe | net bps/day | cost bps/day | net *t* | ~ann. |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **paper (0 cost)** | 0 / 0 | 2.27 | **2.27** | +12.25 | 0.00 | **+7.65** | +30.9% |
| **optimistic** | 5 bp / 20 | 2.27 | **1.39** | +7.51 | 4.74 | +4.69 | +18.9% |
| **realistic** | 10 bp / 50 | 2.27 | **0.24** | +1.27 | 10.98 | **+0.79** | +3.2% |
| **stressed** | 20 bp / 100 | 2.27 | **−1.78** | −9.71 | 21.96 | −5.90 | −24.5% |

The gross Sharpe is identical in every row — it is the *paper* number, blind to trading. The
net Sharpe is the truth: a **dazzling 2.27 on paper**, halved by even optimistic friction,
**statistically dead at a realistic cost** (net *t* = 0.79 < 2), and a **money-loser** when
stressed. The alpha was always an illusion of the missing cost model.

## The break-even cost — the deceptive "headroom"

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| break-even **linear** one-way cost (net alpha → 0) | **35.24 bps** |
| realistic all-in cost charged | ~11 bps/day |

The linear break-even looks comfortable — "we have 35 bps of headroom, a 10 bp cost is fine."
That is exactly the trap: the break-even that ignores **market impact** is a fantasy. Impact
scales with turnover (super-linearly), so at the realistic rung the *actual* daily cost is
10.98 bps against a 12.25 bps gross — the head-room is gone. A break-even quoted without an
impact model is another way of ignoring costs.

## The turnover curve — alpha dies as a FUNCTION of turnover

Hold the gross edge fixed and turn only the turnover knob (φ); charge the **realistic** cost
(10 bp + impact 50) at every point:

| persistence φ | turnover/day | gross Sharpe | net Sharpe | break-even (linear) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.995 | 0.152 | 2.06 | **+1.40** | 72.0 bp |
| 0.98 | 0.254 | 2.15 | **+0.86** | 45.9 bp |
| 0.96 | 0.348 | 2.27 | **+0.24** | 35.2 bp |
| 0.90 | 0.533 | 2.17 | **−1.73** | 22.4 bp |
| 0.70 | 0.893 | 2.21 | **−6.77** | 13.8 bp |
| 0.30 | 1.343 | 2.46 | **−15.54** | 10.0 bp |

The gross Sharpe barely moves (2.06 → 2.46 — the paper alpha is intact everywhere). The **net**
Sharpe falls off a cliff, from a tradable **+1.40** to a catastrophic **−15.54**, and the
break-even cost collapses from 72 bp to 10 bp. *The identical paper alpha is a modest edge at
low turnover and a Mirage at high turnover* — turnover is the axis on which paper meets live.

## Synthetic control — the machinery is unbiased

Gross-book HAC *t* over 20 seeds (a machinery / power check only — never cited for a stamp):

| world | gross *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (`edge = 0`), 20 seeds | mean **+0.01** (sd 0.92), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 1/20** seeds |
| planted (`edge = 0.0005`), 20 seeds | mean **+6.07** (sd 0.92), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 20/20** seeds |

The detector recovers the planted gross edge every time and fires on the null at ~the nominal
5% rate — so the paper alpha is genuinely there to *be* eaten, and the cost gap is real, not a
bug. *(A faithful-engine check only.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** A synthetic-only method demo: the gross edge is planted, not discovered
  on a real tape, so it can never earn `REAL` (which needs a robust *t* ≥ 2 on real data). The
  data-availability limitation is named on the SIGNAL axis and the study is capped at `NONE`.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The 2.27 paper Sharpe is halved by optimistic costs, statistically
  dead at a realistic cost (net *t* = 0.79), and negative when stressed; at anything past
  moderate turnover it is deeply loss-making. There is nothing to harvest once you pay to trade.
- **Does ignoring costs manufacture the edge? — CONFIRMED.** On a strategy with a genuine gross
  edge, dropping the cost model turns a −24%/yr disaster (stressed) or a nothing (+3%/yr,
  realistic) into a +31%/yr triumph on paper. The gap is entirely the cost of trading, it scales
  with turnover, and a break-even quoted without market impact hides it. Report gross *and* net,
  with a turnover-aware cost model — or the backtest is meaningless.
